messages:
daniel: Hey folks — my 2026 YTD withholding on Workday looks wrong. I moved from NY to MA on 2026-04-01 but my W-2 preview still shows NY state withholding for all of 2026. I updated my address in the portal on 2026-04-02. What's the process to correct state wages/withholding on year-end docs?
hr_payroll: Thanks for flagging @daniel. Can you DM a screenshot of the W-2 preview and the address change confirmation? We'll check whether state withholding was applied retroactively or if payroll didn't pick up the address change in the April run.
daniel: DM sent (screenshot + portal history). I only did the address change once I landed in MA and updated the work location accordingly.
payroll-bot: Payroll batch #202606 processed for 2026-06-15; state withholding files submitted to NY and MA.
hr_payroll: Got it. Initial thoughts: likely a timing/mapping issue where the April payroll used the NY state setting before the update propagated, causing NY withholding on April/May. Payroll Ops can investigate and, if needed, reclassify wages and update state tax filings/reports.
finance_ops: Tagging to confirm tax filing impact. If wages were withheld to NY in error, we need to: 1) adjust internal payroll records 2) file a corrected state withholding return (or offset on next return) 3) issue employee refund or adjustment via payroll. We'll need the affected pay dates and amounts.
sam-hr: @daniel please confirm your official work location and whether you had remote days in NY after 2026-04-01 (that might create nexus). Also confirm whether you submitted a new state withholding form (MA Form M-4) or a NY IT-2104 change.
daniel: Official HQ is MA now, no NY days after 2026-04-01. I did not submit a new MA withholding form yet (thought portal update would be enough).
jess-legal: Note for Payroll Ops: if we need to refile or amend NY returns, there may be a short statute window and potential penalties — recommend prompt action and documentation of employee move (lease/travel docs) to support reallocation.
hr_payroll: Plan: 1) Payroll Ops will pull the April/May pay runs and identify state withholding lines 2) If NY was incorrectly used, prepare reversal/adjustment calculations 3) Finance will decide on refund vs. gross-up if tax consequences persist 4) We'll update your W-2 allocation before printing/file submission where possible. Expect first update within 3 business days.
daniel: Appreciate it. Quick question — will this change my year-to-date taxable wages for MA and NY on the W-2? I want to know whether I need to file part-year returns.
finance_ops: Likely yes — if we reclassify wages to MA, your NY wages will decrease and MA wages increase. We'll provide a corrected W-2 or an employee letter explaining adjustments for your tax preparer. If we can't amend before year-end filing, we'll issue corrected W-2 (W-2c) as needed.
payroll-bot: Ticket #PAY-2026-45 created: "Investigate state withholding after midyear move — Daniel" (linked to thread 1784123456). Sensitive attachments stored in People Ops secure bucket.
hr_payroll: Daniel — please upload proof of MA residency (lease or utility bill) to the secure bucket to speed the reallocation.
daniel: Uploaded lease + moving confirmation email.
assumed:  <-- note: placeholder removed in final.
jess-legal: Thanks. We'll keep records in case of state audit. Payroll Ops, coordinate with Finance on any required amended returns and employee notification messaging.
hr_payroll: We'll update this thread by EOD +3 business days with findings. Thanks for the quick docs, @daniel.
daniel: Thanks everyone — glad this is moving.
